findings.title: Error message leaks raw input
findings.body: The error message on line 8 includes the raw input `raw` in the exception text, which could expose sensitive data (e.g., passwords, tokens) if the address is malformed. Use the cleaned value `cleaned` in the message instead.

findings.title: Redundant validation after strip/lower
findings.body: The check `if "@" not in cleaned` is redundant because `strip()` and `lower()` do not remove or alter the `@` character. The validation can be simplified to `if "@" not in raw` or removed entirely if the caller ensures the input is an email address.

summary.problem: The email normalization function introduces a correctness issue by leaking raw input in error messages and a readability issue by performing redundant validation.
summary.done_well: The function now validates that the input contains an '@' character, ensuring basic email format correctness before returning the normalized address.
